target_customer: Clinicians and labs that would order a blood test for symptomatic women to detect ovarian and other gynecologic cancers early; ultimately payers and health systems
problem: No reliable biomarker detects early-stage ovarian cancer; existing diagnostic methods lack sensitivity or specificity per the YC page, so most cases are found late.
business_model: Diagnostics developer: lab-developed or FDA-cleared test sales per test, with a multi-omics discovery platform for other cancers

founders.background_notes: Name spelled inconsistently across sources. Joined full time October 2020 per a profile snippet. Scientific partner Prof. Uri Saragovi of McGill University discovered the underlying approach but is not listed as a founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires discovering and validating glycolipid and multi-omics biomarkers, clinical studies across many sites, and eventual regulatory clearance; research-grade work for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary biomarker panel, clinical data and potential FDA clearance would be hard to replicate, though several diagnostic companies pursue ovarian detection.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an acquisition or copying by 2026; the company continued to present validation data at AACR 2026.

market_need_then: Ovarian cancer is typically detected late and no reliable early-stage biomarker existed per the 2022 funding announcement, a large unmet clinical need.

identity.logo: Company wordmark with Omira product line branding

rebrands.why: Product name change noted in 2026 coverage; reason not sourced

branding.community_and_virality: Trade press coverage of clinical data and a MassNextGen award in 2021; no consumer-facing brand activity found.

brand_strength.rationale: A B2B diagnostics acronym with product-line names; coverage focuses on science and funding, not the brand. The AOA acronym is shared with other entities.

outcome_analysis: AOA Dx raised about $7M in September 2022 and about $17M in October 2023, ran a roughly 1,000-patient validation study and presented results at AACR 2026 while preparing an early access program. The founders had previous diagnostics exits, which helped fundraising credibility. The outcome is still pending regulatory and commercial milestones; the main risk is clinical and regulatory rather than market.
notes: The October 2023 $17M round is labeled seed, Series A or Series B by different sources, so stage is other; Good Growth Capital as lead comes from search snippets of Endpoints and BioWorld (Endpoints returned 403). The 2022 MLSC post gives no stage.
